summary: Iteration 8 — Permissions & Connectors + server.py→routers/* refactor: 40/40 backend tests PASS (100%) in 12.83s on /app/backend/tests/test_iter8_permissions_connectors.py. All 6 review-request areas verified end-to-end against the public preview URL (https://ora-decision-engine.preview.emergentagent.com). (1) REFACTOR REGRESSION — every pre-existing endpoint keeps URL/method/status/shape identical: /api/ root, /auth/register|login|me|logout|google-session (bad token → strict 401), /decisions list|top|GET|POST|dismiss|complete, legacy /priorities & /tasks, /life-graph/vocabulary|seed|nodes, /knowledge/schemas + /knowledge/nodes/{id} (envelope carries 'properties' key), /auto-link/decisions/{id}/analyze + /proposals, /admin/demo/refresh, /memory POST+GET. Google-session with wrong session_token returns 401 — clean. (2) UNIFORM /latest ENVELOPE: strict 4-key envelope {snapshot,status,generated_at,assembler_version} verified in BOTH states — 'available' (after assemble → snapshot!=null, generated_at ISO, assembler_version='context_assembler/v1.0') AND 'not_found' (fresh decision never assembled → snapshot=null, generated_at=null, same version); cross-user (B calls A's decision) returns 404; no-token returns 401/403. (3) node_ids in POST /api/decisions — atomic link with rollback: seeded life graph, picked 2 node ids, POSTed with node_ids=[nid1,nid2] → returned doc has node_ids == {nid1,nid2} AND history contains BOTH 'created' AND 'life_graph.linked' events; passing node_ids=['node_INEXISTENT'] returns 400 AND decision count is byte-identical before/after (rollback confirmed via GET /decisions count delta = 0); POST without node_ids works exactly like before (node_ids null/empty in response); user A passing user B's node id → 400 (ownership check enforced). (4) PERMISSIONS — /api/permissions/*: GET /registry returns {capability_registry_version:'1.0.0', items:[…]} with EXACTLY 11 capabilities; every item carries the 10 required keys (id, connector_domain, verb, data_categories, sensitivity, platforms, requires_oauth, purposes, default_status, enabled); GET /registry/calendar.read → 200, GET /registry/does.not.exist → 404; POST /consents/grant creates doc with status='active'; re-granting the SAME (capability_id, connector_id, connector_instance_id) tuple monotonically increments the version field; GET /consents?status=active includes the tuple; POST /consents/revoke returns doc with status='revoked' AND revoked_at set; post-revoke the tuple is no longer in ?status=active; POST /consents/grant with unknown capability → 404; wildcard grant (connector_instance_id='*') accepted verbatim; POST /consents/revoke-all returns revoked_count>=1 when grants exist; GET /audit yields events containing BOTH 'consent.grant' AND 'consent.revoke' event_types; every audit event exposes event_id, timestamp, retention_until, success, reason_code. PATCH /admin/registry/calendar.read → 403 for a normal user, 200 for demo@ora.app. (5) CONNECTORS — /api/connectors/*: GET /registry returns EXACTLY 14 connectors, each with the 6 required keys (id, category, provider, platforms, required_capabilities, status); all status values ∈ {stub,planned,available,disabled}; GET /registry/calendar_google → 200, unknown → 404; GET /status requires auth (401/403 without token); after granting calendar.read for calendar_google (instance 'primary'), GET /status?connector_id=calendar_google shows summary.granted==1 AND summary.missing_capabilities==[]; the pre-registered stub-only guarantee holds — /connectors/{id}/connect, /oauth, /sync, /webhook all return 404 (both GET and POST). (6) CONTEXT ASSEMBLER + PERMISSIONS PROVIDER (flag default OFF): after POST /context/decisions/{id}/assemble on a fresh decision, provenance.providers_run includes 'permissions' AND the number of signals with source_module=='permissions' is EXACTLY 0; assembling the same decision twice yields byte-identical context_hash (the flag-gated provider does NOT affect the hash when off). Test run flags: pytest -v -n 0 with EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL set.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now a THIN bootstrap file (115 lines) — excellent split. All domain logic lives in /app/backend/routers/*.py (10 routers) and the composite ALL_ROUTERS list drives include_router() in a single loop. No hardcoded URLs; MONGO_URL and CORS from env.

Permissions capability registry uses MappingProxyType to make each capability dict IMMUTABLE at runtime, and _BY_ID uniqueness is asserted at import time — solid defense against runtime tampering. as_dict() correctly explodes MappingProxyType back to a plain dict for JSON serialization (routers/permissions.py:66).

Connectors registry validates at IMPORT TIME that every required_capabilities/optional_capabilities id exists in the permissions registry (connectors/registry.py:237–243). This means a drift between the two registries fails the container startup with a clear RuntimeError — great fail-fast property.

routers/decisions.py create_decision_with_nodes implements atomic composition correctly: validate node ownership BEFORE insert (count_documents with $in + status=active), then decisions.create, then life_graph.link_decision, and on ANY exception delete the just-created decision. Verified empirically: bad node_id returns 400 AND the pre-count == post-count of GET /decisions items.

routers/context.py context_latest returns a STRICT 4-key envelope {snapshot,status,generated_at,assembler_version}. The 404-vs-200 distinction is correct: 404 iff the Decision doesn't belong to the user; 200+status=not_found iff Decision exists but has no snapshot yet. This closes the inconsistency called out in the previous iteration (iteration_8.json action_items[1]).

permissions/service.py grant/revoke/check_access ALL emit an audit event on both success AND failure paths, including reason_code enums (capability_unknown, capability_disabled, granted, no_active_consent). The audit log is append-only and carries retention_until — verified via GET /permissions/audit response contract.

context_assembler/permissions_provider.py is a strict no-op when PERMISSIONS_CONTEXT_ENABLED is unset — returns ProviderResult(name='permissions') with empty signals; verified: provenance.providers_run includes 'permissions' but 0 signals carry source_module=='permissions' and context_hash is byte-stable across two back-to-back assembles of the same decision.

DEMO admin guard uses email allow-list (DEMO_EMAILS in deps) instead of a role field. Simple but effective; verified 403 for a fresh registered user vs 200 for demo@ora.app on PATCH /permissions/admin/registry/{cap_id}.
seed_data_creation: Two ephemeral users per run (iter8a_<ts>_<uuid>@ora.app, iter8b_<ts>_<uuid>@ora.app) via POST /auth/register; module-scoped fixtures. Life graph seeded via POST /life-graph/seed for both users to obtain valid node ids. Demo user (demo@ora.app / Demo!2026) used for admin-guard positive test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Suite runs in ~13s via `EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL=https://ora-decision-engine.preview.emergentagent.com pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iter8_permissions_connectors.py -v -n 0 --tb=short`. Uses module-scoped user_a/user_b/demo_user fixtures — safe under xdist too, but keep -n 0 for log clarity. Field name quirks discovered: (a) google-session body field is `session_token`, NOT `session_id`; (b) history events use key `event` (not `type`); (c) auto-link proposals are per-decision only — no top-level /auto-link/proposals list endpoint (use /auto-link/decisions/{id}/proposals). The 3 pre-existing broken test files noted in iteration_8.json (test_knowledge_layer envelope drift, test_ora_backend seed size, test_ora_decision_engine bracket-lookup) are UNRELATED to iteration 8 and were NOT re-run.
rca_of_issue: N/A — no product bugs. During test authoring three test-only issues surfaced and were fixed inline: (1) google-session body field is `session_token` not `session_id` (Pydantic 422); (2) history events serialize `event` not `type` (see decision_engine/service.py:145); (3) auto-link module exposes per-decision proposal endpoints only, no bare /auto-link/proposals. After these test corrections: 40/40 pass, zero product regressions detected.
